title: Finite freeness of logarithmic differentials at a log-smooth geometric point
statement: Let $f:(X,M)\to(Y,N)$ be a morphism of locally Noetherian fs log schemes [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], log smooth in the chart sense of [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale]. Fix a geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], put $A=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$ and let $R=\mathcal O_{Y,f(\bar x)}$ act on $A$ by $f$. Define $\omega$ to be the $A$-module on symbols $da$ ($a\in A$) and $d\log m$ ($m\in M_{\bar x}$), modulo additivity and the Leibniz rule for $d$, $dc=0$ for $c$ from $R$, $d\log(mm^{\prime})=d\log m+d\log m^{\prime}$, $d\alpha(m)=\alpha(m)d\log m$, and $d\log f^\flat(b)=0$ for $b\in N_{f(\bar x)}$. Then $\omega$ is a finite free $A$-module: there is an integer $s\geq0$ and an $A$-linear isomorphism $\omega\simeq A^s$.

source.place: Expose XVI Proposition 3.6.3 proof, printed p.252, first paragraph of proof (logarithmic differential basis); the general local-freeness input of Kato, Logarithmic structures of Fontaine--Illusie, section 3.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-log-smooth-infinitesimal-calculus] to the given morphism: its hypotheses are exactly locally Noetherian fs source and target and log smoothness in the chart sense. Write $\mathcal W$ for the logarithmic differential sheaf defined in that statement. Its finite-local-freeness clause gives a pointed etale neighbourhood $(U,\bar u)$ of $\bar x$, an integer $s\geq0$, and an isomorphism $e:\mathcal W|_U\simeq\mathcal O_U^s$. This uses only the finite-local-freeness clause, not the infinitesimal lifting assertions. The relations defining $\mathcal W$ are the sheaf versions of exactly the relations defining $\omega$ in this item.

source.place: Expose XVI Proposition 3.6.3 proof, printed p.252, first paragraph; finite-locally-free input supplied by existing lem-per-log-smooth-infinitesimal-calculus; stalk argument supplied by the agent.

proof.text: Identify $\omega$ with $\mathcal W_{\bar x}$ by sending $da$ and $d\log m$ to the germs of the corresponding generators. Here are the generators-and-relations checks. By [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], each germ of a ring or log section has a representative on a pointed etale neighbourhood. By [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods-cofiltered], any finite list of such representatives has a common refinement. Every displayed relation involves finitely many sections, so it holds on a refinement precisely when it holds on germs. For base sections use their representatives at $f(\bar x)$ and restrict to the inverse-image neighbourhood at $\bar x$; thus the base relations are precisely $dc=0$ for $c\in R$ and $d\log f^\flat(b)=0$ for $b\in N_{f(\bar x)}$. Every element of a free module is a finite sum, and membership in the submodule generated by the relations is witnessed by a finite sum of scalar multiples of relations. Hence taking germs before or after imposing the relations gives inverse maps on these finite presentations of individual elements. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-sets-sheafification-geometric-stalk] says that sheafifying this sectionwise presentation does not change its stalk; its bijection respects addition and scalar multiplication since the sheafification map does. The two maps above are therefore inverse $A$-linear maps $\omega\simeq\mathcal W_{\bar x}$.

source.place: Tags 03PQ (lemma-cofinal-etale), 03PT (lemma-stalk-exact), and definition-stalk; explicit finite generators-and-relations argument supplied by the agent.

proof.text: Take germs of $e$ and its inverse on neighbourhoods refining $(U,\bar u)$. These refinements suffice: any neighbourhood can be refined together with $U$ by [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods-cofiltered]. Their composites remain identities on representatives, so $e$ gives $\mathcal W_{\bar x}\simeq(\mathcal O_U^s)_{\bar u}$. The latter module is $A^s$: represent its finitely many coordinate germs simultaneously on one refinement; if two coordinate tuples have the same germs, refine once for each of the finitely many coordinates to obtain equality of the tuples. This is the stalk definition [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], applied coordinatewise, and the same argument identifies $(\mathcal O_U)_{\bar u}$ with $A$. Compose with Step 2 to obtain $\omega\simeq A^s$. For $s=0$ both sides are the zero module and these maps are the unique maps.

Small cases checked: X = A¹ with trivial log structures gives s=1; the identity log morphism gives s=0; the toric chart N gives dt = t·dlog t; empty X is vacuous. Using M rather than M^gp makes no difference. Step 1 cites the existing unsplit node lem-per-log-smooth-infinitesimal-calculus. It is in the same unit and has the same hypotheses (locally Noetherian fs, chart log smoothness) and the same six relations. Its 'finite locally free, étale locally ≅ O_X^s' clause is exactly what the step uses. That node is strictly larger (it adds local finite presentation, lifts and the derivation torsor), so this is C5 reuse, not D1/D2. It has no proof_deps; its citers are only the kato-lattice node and this item, and this item is cited only by the generators node, so there is no cycle. Advisory: the future split of infinitesimal-calculus must not cite this item or the generators node. Lifting x̄ to the étale chart piece is elementary. Steps 2 and 3 compare the presented stalk module with W_x̄ through def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks, the cofilteredness lemma and the sheafification-stalk bijection, all three Mathlib leaves. Each says what is used. Finite sums and finite relation witnesses commute with filtered colimits. The base relations go through the stalks at f(x̄), giving R and N_{f(x̄)}. Finite products of stalks are compared coordinatewise, and s=0 is handled. These steps are elementary. The two lem-weil-pbc-* tool_uses are generic Mathlib-leaf infrastructure, accepted.
